history.new: Not found in any source read (reviews/historian_501.md): the ETP commentary file Equation501.md at HEAD (Sep 12, 2026) says 'The finite spectrum ... of this law is unknown'; B. Le Floch's notes (July 2025) give 'unknown spectrum containing 1,4,5,8,9' and note that x # y = x(xy) obeys law 14; the only exclusions in the sources are order 2 and idempotent models of order = 2 (mod 3) (B. Gunby-Mann, July 14, 2025); no source mentions orders 10-12. The sign identity used for the necessity is a one-line corollary of the classical parity relation pi_r + pi_c + pi_s = C(n,2) (mod 2) for Latin squares (J. C. M. Janssen, JCTA 69 (1995) 173-181; P. Zappa, Boll. UMI 10-A (1996) 63-69; see N. Francetic, S. Herke, I. M. Wanless, JCTA 155 (2018) 67-99, arXiv:1703.04764), since the row, column and symbol parities of a semi-symmetric quasigroup coincide; the semi-symmetric case was not found stated. ETP members may hold unpublished results.

statement: A magma of order n >= 1 satisfying x = y(y(x(xy))) exists if and only if n = 0 or 1 (mod 4). Necessity: x # y = x(xy) is a semi-symmetric quasigroup (law 14) whose left translations are squares L_x^2, hence even, while every finite semi-symmetric quasigroup of order n has prod_y sign(L_y) = (-1)^(n(n-1)/2), because (x, y) -> (y, x # y) has order 3. Sufficiency: on A = Z_n (n odd) or Z_2 x Z_2 x Z_{n/4} (4 | n), x # y = -x - y has involutive translations with an even number of 2-cycles; their square roots sigma_x give the model x * y = sigma_x(y).
title: The spectrum of ETP law 501, x = y(y(x(xy))), is exactly {n : n = 0, 1 (mod 4)}
